title: Vadose Zone Analytical Algorithm Assessment, Conservation Repair & SWAP5 Suitability

primary_source.citation: Sadeghi et al. (2026), Vadose zone analytical algorithm (VZAA): a non-iterative algorithm for vadose zone soil moisture and groundwater recharge, Journal of Hydrology 673, 135467

reason: published coarse-layer examples retain non-negligible cumulative mass-balance residual
published formulation cannot strictly impose the lower zero-flux boundary and therefore does not provide the general prescribed-head/prescribed-flux contract required by SWAP5
published layered-soil case degrades because the analytical flux relation was derived for uniform soil

conservative_modification.required_proof: A bounded correction must close the accepted-step ledger exactly while enforcing the lower interface condition without degenerating into an unbounded global Richards/Newton solve.

candidate_ideas: closed-form or bounded analytical layer updates

reproduce at least one published case without modifying the official implementation
write exact layer-by-layer storage and transfer ledger
construct the smallest conservative bottom-interface correction and prove mass closure algebraically before coding
only if mass and lower-boundary gates pass, compare against full Richards
